item.title: What Ocarina of Time final battle was better: Original or remake? (Spoilers)
item.author: invalid@example.com (Uzumaki Goku)
item.dc:creator: Uzumaki Goku
item.content:encoded: I'm playing both back to back to spot the difference. From the big start of fighting Ganondorf to the end credits. What was better? Both are similar, but differ in some ways. For example, the Remake has no timer to escape which does take away a bit of the tension but does add some cool new set pieces to make up for it such as the Hookshot segment. The final battles are also more elaborate but I prefer the original's lighting for Ganon. So… both have their merit still.

item.title: The way the Ocarina of Time remake changed its in-game economy deserves its own thread
item.author: invalid@example.com (chaobreaker)
item.dc:creator: chaobreaker
item.content:encoded: As someone who has played a lot of Ocarina of Time N64 in the past 28 years, the one change the remake did that shocked me the most was the adjustment of the game's economy. For those who don't know: the original OoT infamously threw you endless rupees—the game world's currency—and you had nothing to spend on it. You were rarely without a maxed out rupee count even when you get the biggest rupee wallet upgrade. There were plenty of effortless and quick methods to make money, like minigames... Read more

item.content:encoded: Whether they're a physical character or just a disembodied voice, radio DJs are one my favourite ways a game can implement world building. They deliver the news, comment on your actions, and set the tone for a game's radio. Often they're the voice we hear most in a game.
